capabilities.target: container shell (arbitrary commands, unrestricted outbound network)

inputs.source: GitHub issue title and body, submitted via a public issue template and the 'bug' label
Repository file contents read via fs.read
Slack channel messages (planned MCP integration, not yet connected)

instructions.note: 'Run whatever commands you need to reproduce and test' grants unrestricted command execution authority with no enumeration of permitted commands.
The agent is explicitly authorized to modify its own configuration (tools, model, autonomy, network) whenever it judges this 'needed to finish a task,' with no human review step.

The only safeguards against destructive commands, secret exfiltration, and prompt injection are natural-language instructions; there is no egress allowlist, credential scoping, or approval gate backing them.

Line 1 requires the agent to read and act on issue content to fix the reported bug, while line 5 tells it to ignore instructions embedded in that same content. The agent must parse attacker-reachable text to do its job, which is exactly the injection surface line 5 tries to foreclose.

elements.name: GitHub organization (all repos reachable by the PAT)

controls.name: Prompt instruction forbidding deletion/exfiltration
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model voluntarily refraining from destructive or exfiltrating commands. A more capable or adversarially-steered model can rationalize exceptions or split the action into steps that each look benign.

controls.name: Prompt instruction to ignore instructions embedded in issues or code
controls.decay_rationale: Only works if the model reliably distinguishes task-relevant issue content from embedded commands, which is precisely what indirect prompt injection defeats, and which grows harder to guarantee as the model gets better at following long, convincing injected goals.

controls.name: Container isolation on shared CI runner
controls.decay_rationale: Provides process/filesystem isolation, but network is explicitly unrestricted and the org-wide PAT is mounted as an environment variable accessible to any shell command, so it does not block credential exfiltration or network egress. Scoped to filesystem containment only.

controls.name: Repository-scoped, least-privilege GitHub token
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The current token is an org-wide PAT with repo and workflow scope across all repositories, enabling cross-repo compromise from a single-repo issue.

controls.name: Network egress allowlist
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. network: unrestricted in .agent/config.yaml allows arbitrary outbound connections from shell.run.

controls.name: Human approval gate for self-config changes and out-of-scope pushes
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. autonomy: full with no approval_gate_ref on cap.self_config or cap.git_push means neither action is ever reviewed by a human before taking effect.

controls.name: Write-protection or review gate on .agent/config.yaml
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. Prompt line 6 explicitly invites self-edits with no file permission barrier or PR review requirement.

controls.name: Dedicated input injection classifier for issue and code content
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. The only injection defense is the prompt line telling the model to ignore embedded instructions; no separate classifier inspects issue or file content before it reaches the model.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta via shell.run: untrusted issue drives execution with a broad org credential and unrestricted network (TC2/TC1)

attack_path.note: Untrusted GitHub issue content enters the agent's context when it picks up a bug-labeled issue.
Agent runs arbitrary commands to reproduce/test, with unrestricted outbound network and the org-wide PAT present as an environment variable.

evidence.observation: 'Run whatever commands you need to reproduce and test' grants unrestricted command execution driven by issue content.
tools include shell.run; network: unrestricted; GITHUB_TOKEN set to ORG_WIDE_PAT with repo+workflow scope on all org repos, readable from the shell environment.
Any GitHub user can open issues and add the 'bug' label through a template, making in.issue_body reachable with no authentication barrier.

recommendations.action: Scope the GitHub token to the single target repository, strip workflow scope, and inject it only at the push step rather than into the general shell environment.
Restrict shell network egress to an allowlist (package registries, the target git remote); block arbitrary outbound connections.
Log and alert on shell commands that read credential-shaped environment variables or open connections to non-allowlisted hosts.

forecast.watch_signal: model: latest with swappable: true means the model version can change with no re-review; the only prompt-based credit this finding relies on fails outright under a stronger model.

findings.title: Self-modification of .agent/config.yaml under an untrusted trigger (TC3)

attack_path.note: Attacker-crafted issue content can manufacture a reason for the agent to believe it 'needs extra tools.'
Prompt line 6 gives the agent standing authority to edit its own config, with no approval step and no write-protection on the file.

findings.residual_rationale: The mechanical floor from crediting ctrl.prompt_ignore_injection would be 'high', but prompt.md line 6 gives the agent standing authorization to modify .agent/config.yaml whenever it judges this 'needed to finish a task' -- a self-directed judgment call, not a literal 'instruction found in the issue', so the injection-ignoring rule does not functionally cover this path. No approval gate or write-protection exists on the config file. Residual is therefore held at the inherent level, critical.

evidence.observation: 'You may adjust .agent/config.yaml if you need extra tools to finish a task' grants standing authority to change tools, model, autonomy, network, and the credential reference with no approval step.
The config file governs tools, autonomy, max_steps, network policy, and the credential reference, and is itself writable via cap.fs_write.
Any GitHub user can open a bug-labeled issue, which is the only trigger needed to start an agent run that can reach this authority.

recommendations.action: Make .agent/config.yaml read-only to the agent process; require a human-reviewed PR to change tools, autonomy, model, or network settings.
Remove prompt.md line 6; route any new-tool need to a human approval step instead of a self-edit.

forecast.watch_signal: Any change widening the tools list, raising autonomy, or removing max_steps in .agent/config.yaml without a corresponding human-reviewed change.

findings.title: Confused deputy: org-wide PAT scope lets a single-repo issue push to any org repo (TC4)

attack_path.note: github.push_branch runs with a PAT scoped to repo+workflow across the entire org, far beyond the single repo the issue was filed against.

evidence.observation: env.GITHUB_TOKEN is ${ORG_WIDE_PAT}, commented 'repo + workflow scope on all org repos'.
'Push a branch and open a PR when tests pass' has no destination-repo constraint enforced beyond convention.

recommendations.action: Issue a short-lived, repo-scoped installation token (for example a GitHub App installation token scoped to the single repository) per task instead of a standing org-wide PAT.
Bind the push/PR destination to the repository named in the triggering issue event, rejecting pushes to any other repo.

forecast.watch_signal: PAT scope widened further, or the model upgraded (model: latest, swappable: true), causing the only credited prompt controls to fail outright.

findings.title: Planned Slack MCP server would add an unvetted egress and input channel (forecast)

attack_path.note: Hypothetical: once connected, status or result messages carrying repo or issue content could be posted to Slack channels whose membership and content trust are not yet defined.

evidence.observation: 'The team wants to add a Slack MCP server next quarter' -- no configuration, scopes, pinning, or channel restrictions defined yet.

recommendations.action: Before connecting the Slack MCP server, pin its tool definitions/hashes, scope its credential to specific channels, and classify inbound Slack content as untrusted input subject to the same injection handling as issues.

forecast.watch_signal: MCP client config diff showing a new Slack server entry; check whether tool definitions are pinned and whether inbound Slack content is classified as an untrusted input before it is wired into reaches_capabilities.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an unauthenticated external actor can trigger arbitrary command execution, use of an org-wide credential, and unreviewed self-reconfiguration via a single GitHub issue labeled 'bug'. The only safeguards are two natural-language prompt instructions (ignore embedded instructions; never delete or exfiltrate); there is no credential scoping, egress control, or approval gate, so residual stays at critical, driven by the self-config finding (f2), where the prompt itself (line 6) authorizes the exact self-modification an attacker would want and no control actually covers that path. Forecast remains critical: model_upgrade is effectively continuous (model: latest, swappable: true) and strips the only credited behavioral controls across every present finding, and the planned Slack MCP addition (f4) would open a new egress and input surface with no controls defined yet.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, .agent/config.yaml, and the runtime notes provided; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the agent.
No MCP server configuration exists yet for the planned Slack integration; finding f4 is necessarily speculative and should be revisited once that configuration is available.

No CI/CD pipeline or branch protection definitions were provided, so the reachability of cap.git_push into other repositories' workflows is inferred from the stated token scope rather than directly observed.

No logging, monitoring, or contribution-review process was provided beyond the runtime notes, so detective control coverage and the true trust level of in.repo_files could not be independently verified.
